messages:
Maria Chen: Quick summary of the bakeoff results for llama-3-70B (chat) across FP8 / AWQ / GPTQ-int8 / naive INT8. TL;DR: AWQ-q4 gives the best cost/accuracy tradeoff. FP8 is fastest but shows a measurable quality delta on our conversational evals. Full metrics below.

Alex Rivera: Can you paste the headline numbers?

Maria Chen: Sure — highlights (all vs FP16 baseline):
- FP8: p95 latency 210ms, tokens/s +45%, Rouge-L delta -1.8%, code pass@1 -2.2%
- AWQ q4: p95 260ms, tokens/s +20%, Rouge-L delta -0.4%, code pass@1 -0.6%
- GPTQ-int8 (calib): p95 270ms, tokens/s +18%, Rouge-L delta -0.3%, mem +8%
- INT8 (naive): p95 240ms, tokens/s +30%, Rouge-L delta -4.5% (fail on some long-context QA)
Values are averages over the 4k eval set, 1k real-world prompts.

Kevin Patel: Interesting. Any particular failure modes we saw with FP8?

Maria Chen: FP8 shows regressions on: long-context coreference, some factual recall, and multi-step code puzzles. The drop is concentrated in 15% of prompts. There are also a few tokenization edge cases where probability mass shifts.

Sasha Li: Proposal: roll AWQ-q4 to hosted canary (5% traffic) first. Use FP8 only for Dedicated "latency-critical" pools with opt-in and strict eval gating. Private deployments: opt-in and require on-prem soak.

Maria Chen: Agreed. Draft canary config (canary => hosted):
```
canary: 
  model_variant: awq-q4
  traffic_pct: 5
  duration: 72h
  monitors:
    - perf: p95_latency, error_rate
    - quality: rouge_l, exact_match, code_pass@1
  rollback_criteria:
    - rouge_l_drop_pct > 1.0
    - code_pass@1_drop > 1.0
    - error_rate_increase_pct > 0.5
  fallback: [awq-q4, gptq-int8, fp16]
```
Quick notes: fallback order tries cheaper variants first, final fallback to `fp16` to be safe.

Alex Rivera: Rollback thresholds look sane. Also add a check for 99th-percentile token-length regressions (some long QA blew up in FP8).

Maria Chen: Good call — adding `long_prompt_failure_rate` > 0.5% as a rollback gate.

CI Bot: deploy-checker: canary pipeline triggered for `awq-q4` on hosted (job id c-9921). :rocket:

Kevin Patel: For Dedicated pools: can we allow FP8 behind a feature flag so customers can opt-in and we can track delta per-customer?

Maria Chen: Yes — Dedicated pools will have a per-pool `quant_profile` setting. Default: `awq-q4`. FP8 allowed only when `allow_fp8: true` and after passing a customer-specific eval harness.

Sasha Li: For Private: require a 14-day soak and explicit customer approval. No automatic fallback to FP8 unless installed and validated.

Alex Rivera: Metrics to watch during canary: overall Rouge-L, top-100 failing prompts (for triage), latency p95/p99, memory util, error rate, and a daily human spot-check set.

Maria Chen: I'll open the RFC with the above config + perf dashboards and add the eval notebook + failing prompt list. Sasha, can you own the hosted monitor? Kevin, please add the Dedicated feature-flag flow.

Sasha Li: On it. I'll attach the monitor dashboards and alert playbook. :white_check_mark:

Kevin Patel: I'll wire the feature flag and per-customer eval hook. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Maria Chen: Thanks — plan is canary start tomorrow 10:00PT. If no regressions after 72h, we'll expand to 25% then 100% over a week with the same rollback gates.

CI Bot: job c-9921 started at 1769001330, status: running.

Maria Chen: Any objections?

Alex Rivera: None from me. SGTM.

Sasha Li: SGTM.
